creators.name: Mathieu Lehanneur
creators.role: Designer; founder of Studio Mathieu Lehanneur
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Studio Mathieu Lehanneur 创始人
creators.bio: French designer who works across objects, interiors and science collaborations; early projects paired domestic products with plants, algae and fish.
creators.bio_zh: 法国设计师，作品横跨产品、室内与科学合作；早期项目把家居用品与植物、藻类和鱼组合在一起。
creators.why: Bel-Air, Local River and the O oxygen generator made living organisms part of household appliances well before bio design had a name.
creators.why_zh: Bel-Air、Local River 和 O 制氧器在“生物设计”这个说法出现之前，就把活的生物做进了家用电器。

creators.name: Tobie Kerridge
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Goldsmiths, University of London
creators.role_zh: 设计师与研究者，伦敦大学金史密斯学院
creators.bio: British designer who studied in the Royal College of Art Design Interactions programme and researches public engagement with science through design.
creators.bio_zh: 英国设计师，毕业于皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 专业，研究如何用设计让公众参与科学。
creators.why: Biojewellery was one of the first design projects to hand tissue engineering to ordinary couples as a material for personal objects.
creators.why_zh: Biojewellery 是最早把组织工程交给普通情侣、用来制作私人物件的设计项目之一。

creators.name: James King
creators.role: Designer; Royal College of Art Design Interactions graduate
creators.role_zh: 设计师；皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 专业毕业
creators.bio: British designer whose graduate work at the Royal College of Art speculated on how lab-grown meat might look and be served.
creators.bio_zh: 英国设计师，在皇家艺术学院的毕业作品思考了实验室培育的肉会长什么样、怎样上桌。
creators.why: Dressing the Meat of Tomorrow turned in-vitro meat into a question of form and culture, not only of technology.
creators.why_zh: Dressing the Meat of Tomorrow 把体外培育肉变成了关于造型和文化的问题，而不只是技术问题。

creators.name: Elio Caccavale
creators.role: Designer; Royal College of Art Design Interactions graduate
creators.role_zh: 设计师；皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 专业毕业
creators.bio: Italian designer who works with scientists and ethicists on objects that help people, especially children, talk about biotechnology.
creators.bio_zh: 意大利设计师，与科学家和伦理学者合作，设计帮助人们（尤其是孩子）讨论生物技术的物件。
creators.why: His MyBio toys made transgenic and cloned animals into household companions to open a conversation about genetic engineering.
creators.why_zh: 他的 MyBio 玩偶把转基因和克隆动物做成家中的玩伴，用来打开关于基因工程的讨论。

creators.name: Agata Jaworska
creators.role: Designer and curator; Design Academy Eindhoven graduate
creators.role_zh: 设计师与策展人；埃因霍温设计学院毕业
creators.bio: Polish-Canadian designer whose graduation project Made in Transit proposed food that grows during shipping instead of spoiling.
creators.bio_zh: 波兰裔加拿大设计师，毕业作品 Made in Transit 提出让食物在运输途中生长，而不是在途中变质。
creators.why: Made in Transit reframed packaging as a growth chamber for fungi, an early design case of living products in the supply chain.
creators.why_zh: Made in Transit 把包装重新定义为真菌的生长室，是供应链中“活产品”的早期设计案例。

creators.name: Michael Burton
creators.role: Designer; co-founder of the studio Burton Nitta
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Burton Nitta 工作室联合创始人
creators.bio: British designer from the Royal College of Art Design Interactions programme who, with Michiko Nitta, makes speculative projects on bodies, biotechnology and the environment.
creators.bio_zh: 英国设计师，出自皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 专业，与 Michiko Nitta 合作，创作关于身体、生物技术与环境的思辨项目。
creators.why: His Future Farm projects imagined the human body itself as a site for growing biological products and microbes.
creators.why_zh: 他的 Future Farm 系列把人的身体本身想象成培育生物产品和微生物的场所。

creators.name: Auger-Loizeau
creators.role: Design studio of James Auger and Jimmy Loizeau
creators.role_zh: James Auger 与 Jimmy Loizeau 的设计工作室
creators.bio: Speculative design partnership formed in 2000 by two Royal College of Art graduates, known for prototypes that question how technology enters everyday life.
creators.bio_zh: 两位皇家艺术学院毕业生于 2000 年组建的思辨设计搭档，以质疑技术如何进入日常生活的原型闻名。
creators.why: Augmented Animals asked what technology would look like if it were designed for animals' needs rather than people's.
creators.why_zh: Augmented Animals 追问：如果技术是按动物而不是人的需要来设计，会是什么样子。

creators.name: Fernando Laposse
creators.role: Designer; founder of Studio Fernando Laposse
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Studio Fernando Laposse 创始人
creators.bio: Mexican designer who turns plant fibres such as corn husk, sisal and loofah into materials, often through long projects with rural communities.
creators.bio_zh: 墨西哥设计师，把玉米苞叶、剑麻和丝瓜络等植物纤维做成材料，常与乡村社区长期合作。
creators.why: Totomoxtle links a material to seed conservation and farming practice, not only to a product.
creators.why_zh: Totomoxtle 把一种材料和种子保育、农耕实践联系在一起，而不只是做成一件产品。

creators.name: Nervous System
creators.role: Generative design studio of Jessica Rosenkrantz and Jesse Louis-Rosenberg
creators.role_zh: Jessica Rosenkrantz 与 Jesse Louis-Rosenberg 的生成式设计工作室
creators.bio: Studio that writes simulations of natural growth processes to generate jewellery, textiles and objects, and collaborates with scientists on biofabrication.
creators.bio_zh: 编写自然生长过程模拟程序来生成首饰、织物和物件的工作室，也与科学家合作做生物制造。
creators.why: Their work with Jordan Miller's lab brought generative design into printing vascular networks for engineered tissue.
creators.why_zh: 他们与 Jordan Miller 实验室的合作，把生成式设计带进了为工程组织打印血管网络的研究。

creators.name: Sam Van Aken
creators.role: Artist; Professor of Art, Syracuse University
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；雪城大学艺术教授
creators.bio: American artist who uses grafting to preserve heirloom fruit varieties in living sculptural trees.
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用嫁接把传统水果品种保存在一棵棵有雕塑感的活树上。
creators.why: The Tree of 40 Fruit turns an old horticultural craft into living art and a seed bank for rare varieties.
creators.why_zh: Tree of 40 Fruit 把一门古老的园艺手艺变成活的艺术，也变成稀有品种的基因库。

creators.name: Jae Rhim Lee
creators.role: Artist; founder of Coeio
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；Coeio 创始人
creators.bio: Korean-American artist who started the Infinity Burial Project and founded Coeio to produce a mushroom-based burial suit.
creators.bio_zh: 韩裔美国艺术家，发起 Infinity Burial Project，并创立 Coeio 生产以蘑菇为基础的安葬服。
creators.why: The Infinity Burial Suit designs death as a relationship with fungi and soil.
creators.why_zh: Infinity Burial Suit 把死亡设计成与真菌和土壤的一段关系。

creators.name: DnA_Design and Architecture
creators.role: Architecture office led by Xu Tiantian
creators.role_zh: 由徐甜甜主持的建筑事务所
creators.bio: Beijing architecture office known for small rural interventions in Songyang County and for landscape-scale projects that reuse existing structures.
creators.bio_zh: 北京的建筑事务所，以松阳县的小型乡村介入项目和利用既有结构的景观尺度项目闻名。
creators.why: Its Bamboo Theatre and Into the Island show architecture built with living plants and minimal intervention in ecosystems.
creators.why_zh: 竹剧场和《Into the Island》展示了用活体植物建造、尽量少干预生态系统的建筑。

creators.name: Suomi/Koivisto Architects
creators.role: Architecture practice of Maiju Suomi and Elina Koivisto
creators.role_zh: Maiju Suomi 与 Elina Koivisto 的建筑事务所
creators.bio: Finnish architects working on landscape, natural building materials and practice-led research at Aalto University into architecture for more-than-human communities.
creators.bio_zh: 芬兰建筑师，关注景观与天然建材，并在阿尔托大学以实践为导向研究面向超越人类群落的建筑。
creators.why: The Alusta Pavilion is a built test of architecture designed as habitat for insects, plants and soil fungi as well as people.
creators.why_zh: Alusta 展亭是一次实建检验：建筑同时作为昆虫、植物、土壤真菌和人的栖所。

creators.name: SCAPE Landscape Architecture
creators.role: Landscape architecture office founded by Kate Orff
creators.role_zh: 由 Kate Orff 创立的景观建筑事务所
creators.bio: New York landscape practice known for coastal resilience projects that combine storm protection with habitat and community programmes.
creators.bio_zh: 纽约的景观事务所，以把防风暴、栖息地营造和社区项目结合在一起的海岸韧性项目闻名。
creators.why: Living Breakwaters shows infrastructure designed as oyster and fish habitat at city scale.
creators.why_zh: Living Breakwaters 展示了在城市尺度上被设计成牡蛎和鱼类栖息地的基础设施。

creators.name: Parsons & Charlesworth
creators.role: Speculative design studio of Tim Parsons and Jessica Charlesworth
creators.role_zh: Tim Parsons 与 Jessica Charlesworth 的思辨设计工作室
creators.bio: Chicago studio making speculative objects, drawings and fictional organisations about climate futures; both teach at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.
creators.bio_zh: 芝加哥工作室，用思辨物件、绘画和虚构机构探讨气候未来；两人都在芝加哥艺术学院任教。
creators.why: Multispecies Inc. imagines the tools and bureaucracy of an organisation charged with helping all species flourish.
creators.why_zh: Multispecies Inc. 想象了一家以“让所有物种繁荣”为使命的机构会有怎样的工具和官僚体系。

creators.name: Johanna Seelemann
creators.role: Designer; founder of Studio Johanna Seelemann
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Studio Johanna Seelemann 创始人
creators.bio: German designer working between product design, material research and speculative projects on consumption and ecology.
creators.bio_zh: 德国设计师，在产品设计、材料研究以及关于消费与生态的思辨项目之间工作。
creators.why: Her habitat façades and clay irrigation vessels show product design written for birds, insects and plants.
creators.why_zh: 她的栖息立面和陶土灌溉器，展示了为鸟、昆虫和植物而写的产品设计。

creators.name: Ant Farm
creators.role: Architecture, graphic arts and environmental design collective (1968–1978)
creators.role_zh: 建筑、平面艺术与环境设计团体（1968–1978）
creators.bio: Radical collective founded by Chip Lord and Doug Michels, later joined by Curtis Schreier, known for Cadillac Ranch, inflatables and media performances.
creators.bio_zh: 由 Chip Lord 和 Doug Michels 创立、后有 Curtis Schreier 加入的激进团体，以 Cadillac Ranch、充气结构和媒体表演闻名。
creators.why: Its Dolphin Embassy is an early architectural proposal for communication and cohabitation with another intelligent species.
creators.why_zh: 它的 Dolphin Embassy 是较早的建筑提案，设想与另一种智慧物种交流和共居。

creators.name: Corentin Mahieu
creators.role: Designer; co-founder of Bento Architecture
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Bento Architecture 联合创始人
creators.bio: Belgian designer working with wood, waste streams and mycelium on furniture and interiors.
creators.bio_zh: 比利时设计师，用木材、废料和菌丝体制作家具和室内作品。
creators.why: Accalmie grows mycelium on the offcuts of its own wooden base, keeping the fungus dormant but able to regrow for repairs.
creators.why_zh: Accalmie 让菌丝体长在自身木质底座的边角料上，菌丝处于休眠状态，但修补时可以再次生长。

creators.name: Marlène Huissoud
creators.role: Designer and artist
creators.role_zh: 设计师与艺术家
creators.bio: French designer, raised by a beekeeper, who works with insect by-products such as propolis and silkworm cocoons and designs habitats for insects.
creators.bio_zh: 在养蜂人家庭长大的法国设计师，使用蜂胶、蚕茧等昆虫副产品，并为昆虫设计栖息结构。
creators.why: Her work moves from using insect materials to designing furniture whose users are insects.
creators.why_zh: 她的作品从使用昆虫材料，走到了设计以昆虫为使用者的家具。

creators.name: César Rodríguez-Garavito
creators.role: Professor of Law, NYU School of Law; founding director of the More-Than-Human Life (MOTH) Program
creators.role_zh: 纽约大学法学院法学教授；More-Than-Human Life（MOTH）项目创始主任
creators.bio: Colombian legal scholar and field lawyer working on the rights of nature, climate litigation and Earth rights.
creators.bio_zh: 哥伦比亚法学学者与一线律师，研究自然权利、气候诉讼和地球权利。
creators.why: MOTH connects law, science and art to give rivers, forests and animals legal standing.
creators.why_zh: MOTH 把法律、科学和艺术连在一起，为河流、森林和动物争取法律地位。

creators.name: Tomáš Gabzdil Libertíny
creators.role: Artist and designer
creators.bio: Slovak-born, Netherlands-based artist who makes sculptures and vessels by letting honeybees build comb over prepared forms.
creators.why: He treats bees as co-makers and calls the process 'slow prototyping'.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、设计师
creators.bio_zh: 出生于斯洛伐克、在荷兰工作的艺术家，让蜜蜂在预先准备好的形体上筑巢，做成雕塑和器皿。
creators.why_zh: 他把蜜蜂当作共同制作者，把这种过程称为“慢速原型”。

creators.name: Carlos Peralta
creators.role: Design researcher; Design in Science project, Institute for Manufacturing, University of Cambridge
creators.bio: Carlos Peralta is a design researcher who worked with Cambridge scientists on how design can communicate emerging science, including biophotovoltaics.
creators.why: His Moss Table made plant-powered electricity tangible as a piece of domestic furniture.
creators.role_zh: 设计研究者；剑桥大学制造研究所 Design in Science 项目
creators.bio_zh: Carlos Peralta 是设计研究者，与剑桥科学家合作，研究设计如何传达新兴科学，包括生物光伏。
creators.why_zh: 他的 Moss Table 把植物发电变成了一件可触摸的家具。

creators.name: IDEO
creators.role: Design and innovation consultancy
creators.bio: Global design consultancy; its San Francisco studio ran early speculative projects with synthetic biologists.
creators.why: Its 'Packaging That Creates Its Contents' was an early industrial-design take on synthetic biology.
creators.role_zh: 设计与创新咨询公司
creators.bio_zh: 全球性设计咨询公司，其旧金山工作室较早与合成生物学家合作做思辨项目。
creators.why_zh: 它的“会生成内容物的包装”是工业设计较早介入合成生物学的尝试之一。

creators.name: Vincent Fournier
creators.role: Photographer and artist
creators.bio: French photographer whose series look at space exploration, robots and imagined future life forms.
creators.why: Post Natural History documents animals redesigned by synthetic biology as if they were museum specimens.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法国摄影师，作品关注太空探索、机器人和想象中的未来生命形态。
creators.why_zh: 《Post Natural History》把被合成生物学重新设计的动物拍成博物馆标本一样的档案。

creators.name: Christian Kerrigan
creators.role: Artist and architect
creators.bio: Christian Kerrigan is an artist-architect who draws and films with growing and self-organising matter, including protocells and trees.
creators.why: He uses chemically 'lifelike' protocells as a drawing tool.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: Christian Kerrigan 是艺术家兼建筑师，用会生长、会自组织的物质（包括原细胞和树木）来绘画和拍片。
creators.why_zh: 他把具有“类生命”行为的化学原细胞当作画笔。

creators.name: Shamees Aden
creators.role: Biodesigner and materials researcher
creators.bio: Shamees Aden is a London designer who works with scientists on living and protocell-based materials for fashion and sportswear.
creators.why: Her Amoeba shoe imagines footwear that grows and repairs itself around the runner's foot.
creators.role_zh: 生物设计师、材料研究者
creators.bio_zh: Shamees Aden 是伦敦设计师，与科学家合作研究用于时尚和运动装备的活体材料和原细胞材料。
creators.why_zh: 她的 Amoeba 跑鞋设想一双会围绕跑者的脚生长、自我修复的鞋。

creators.name: Troika
creators.role: Art and design studio (Eva Rucki, Conny Freyer, Sebastien Noel)
creators.bio: London art collective making installations and speculative objects about perception, technology and nature.
creators.why: Plant Fiction imagined engineered plant species that repair the damage of urban life.
creators.role_zh: 艺术与设计工作室（Eva Rucki、Conny Freyer、Sebastien Noel）
creators.bio_zh: 伦敦艺术团体，创作关于感知、技术与自然的装置和思辨物件。
creators.why_zh: 《Plant Fiction》设想了几种能修补城市生活后果的工程植物。

creators.name: Clive van Heerden
creators.role: Designer; former head of Philips Design Probes; co-founder of Van Heerden Mama
creators.bio: Clive van Heerden led the Philips Design Probes programme, which produced the Microbial Home, and later made speculative design films with Jack Mama and Nancy Tilbury.
creators.why: His probes put microbes and biotechnology into everyday domestic scenarios to test how people feel about them.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；飞利浦设计 Design Probes 项目前负责人；Van Heerden Mama 联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: Clive van Heerden 曾领导飞利浦设计的 Design Probes 项目（Microbial Home 即出自这里），之后与 Jack Mama、Nancy Tilbury 合作拍摄思辨设计影片。
creators.why_zh: 他的设计探针把微生物和生物技术放进日常家居场景，测试人们对它们的感受。

creators.name: Jenny E. Sabin
creators.role: Architect; Professor of Architecture, Cornell University; principal of Jenny Sabin Studio
creators.bio: Jenny Sabin is an architect who works across architecture, cell biology and materials science, building adaptive structures from insights into how cells behave.
creators.why: Her LabStudio with Peter Lloyd Jones and the eSkin project brought wet-lab cell biology into architectural research.
creators.role_zh: 建筑师；康奈尔大学建筑学教授；Jenny Sabin Studio 负责人
creators.bio_zh: Jenny Sabin 是横跨建筑、细胞生物学和材料科学的建筑师，从细胞行为中获得启发来建造自适应结构。
creators.why_zh: 她与 Peter Lloyd Jones 合办的 LabStudio 及 eSkin 项目，把湿实验室的细胞生物学带进了建筑研究。

creators.name: Ann-Kristin Abel
creators.role: Designer; MA Textile Futures, Central Saint Martins
creators.bio: Ann-Kristin Abel is a designer who made speculative films about semi-living devices while studying at Central Saint Martins.
creators.why: The Plasmorph imagines a wearable semi-living organism that feeds information directly to the body.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Central Saint Martins 纺织未来硕士
creators.bio_zh: Ann-Kristin Abel 是设计师，在 Central Saint Martins 求学期间拍摄了关于半活体装置的思辨影片。
creators.why_zh: 《The Plasmorph》设想一种可佩戴的半活体生物，把信息直接输送给身体。

creators.name: David Benqué
creators.role: Designer and researcher; Design Interactions graduate, Royal College of Art
creators.bio: David Benqué is a French designer and researcher whose work looks at diagrams, prediction and the politics of science and technology.
creators.why: The New Weathermen imagines eco-activists who use synthetic biology as a tool of direct action.
creators.role_zh: 设计师、研究者；皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 毕业
creators.bio_zh: David Benqué 是法国设计师和研究者，关注图表、预测以及科学技术中的政治。
creators.why_zh: 《The New Weathermen》设想一群把合成生物学当作直接行动工具的环保激进分子。

creators.name: Koby Barhard
creators.role: Designer; Design Interactions graduate, Royal College of Art
creators.bio: Koby Barhard is an Israeli-born designer whose speculative projects use commercially available biotech services to test ideas about identity and heredity.
creators.why: All That I Am shows that anyone can order transgenic mice modelled on a celebrity's DNA.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；皇家艺术学院 Design Interactions 毕业
creators.bio_zh: Koby Barhard 是出生于以色列的设计师，他的思辨项目利用市面上可买到的生物技术服务，检验关于身份与遗传的观念。
creators.why_zh: 《All That I Am》表明，任何人都可以按照名人的 DNA 订购转基因小鼠。

creators.name: Mae-ling Lokko
creators.role: Architectural scientist, designer and artist; Assistant Professor, Yale School of Architecture; founder of Willow Technologies
creators.bio: Ghanaian-Filipino architectural scientist who upcycles agricultural waste, fungi and plant fibres into building materials, linking material research to generative justice.
creators.why: Her mycelium and agro-waste structures treat waste streams and fungi as the basis of a fairer building economy.
creators.role_zh: 建筑科学家、设计师、艺术家；耶鲁大学建筑学院助理教授；Willow Technologies 创始人
creators.based_zh: 纽黑文，美国 / 阿克拉，加纳
creators.bio_zh: 加纳-菲律宾裔建筑科学家，把农业废弃物、真菌和植物纤维升级再造为建筑材料，并把材料研究与“生成性正义”联系起来。
creators.why_zh: 她的菌丝体与农业废料结构，把废弃物流和真菌当作更公平的建造经济的基础。

creators.name: Kristel Peters
creators.role: Shoe designer; Studio COJAK
creators.bio: Belgian footwear designer who grew shoe prototypes from fungal mycelium for Officina Corpuscoli's Fungal Futures exhibition.
creators.why: She tested how far mycelium can replace leather and foam in a shoe.
creators.role_zh: 鞋类设计师；Studio COJAK
creators.bio_zh: 比利时鞋类设计师，为 Officina Corpuscoli 的 Fungal Futures 展用真菌菌丝体长出鞋子原型。
creators.why_zh: 她测试了菌丝体能在多大程度上替代鞋中的皮革和泡棉。

creators.name: The Mycological Twist
creators.role: Artist collective (Eloïse Bonneviot and Anne de Boer)
creators.bio: An art project by Eloïse Bonneviot and Anne de Boer that runs a mushroom garden and a nomadic programme of works, talks and performances timed to inoculation, growth and harvest.
creators.why: It makes a fungal garden, not a white cube, the organising structure of an art programme.
creators.role_zh: 艺术团体（Eloïse Bonneviot 与 Anne de Boer）
creators.bio_zh: 由 Eloïse Bonneviot 和 Anne de Boer 发起的艺术项目，经营一座蘑菇花园，并按接种、生长和采收的节奏安排巡回的作品、讲座和表演。
creators.why_zh: 它让一座真菌花园（而不是白盒子展厅）成为整个艺术项目的组织结构。

creators.name: Joris Laarman
creators.role: Designer; founder of Joris Laarman Lab and co-founder of MX3D
creators.bio: Dutch designer known for furniture generated by algorithms and robotic 3D metal printing, who has also experimented with biological materials.
creators.why: His Half Life lamp was an early design object made of genetically modified living cells.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Joris Laarman Lab 创始人、MX3D 联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰设计师，以算法生成的家具和机器人金属 3D 打印著称，也做过生物材料实验。
creators.why_zh: 他的 Half Life 灯是较早由转基因活细胞构成的设计物件之一。

creators.name: Hongjie Yang
creators.role: Designer; Design Academy Eindhoven graduate
creators.bio: Chinese designer based in the Netherlands who works with tissue engineers on objects partly made of living human cells.
creators.why: His Semi-Human Vase asks what it means to own and display an object grown from human cells.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；埃因霍温设计学院毕业
creators.bio_zh: 在荷兰工作的中国设计师，与组织工程研究者合作，制作部分由活体人类细胞构成的物件。
creators.why_zh: 他的《Semi-Human Vase》追问：拥有并陈列一件由人类细胞长成的物件意味着什么。

creators.name: Gabriela Munguía
creators.role: Artist and researcher
creators.bio: Mexican artist who builds printed micro-architectures and measuring devices to study how microorganisms inhabit and change urban space.
creators.why: Her work treats the city as a biological organisation shared with microbes.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者
creators.bio_zh: 墨西哥艺术家，搭建打印出来的微型建筑和测量装置，研究微生物如何栖居并改变城市空间。
creators.why_zh: 她把城市看作与微生物共享的生物组织。

creators.name: Jen Bervin
creators.role: Poet and visual artist
creators.bio: American poet and artist whose books and installations work across text and textile, including collaborations with silk-materials scientists.
creators.why: The Silk Poems uses silk as both subject and medium: a poem nanoimprinted on a silk biosensor meant for the body.
creators.role_zh: 诗人、视觉艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国诗人和艺术家，作品横跨文本与织物，包括与蚕丝材料科学家的合作。
creators.why_zh: 《The Silk Poems》把蚕丝同时当作主题和媒介：一首诗被纳米压印在可植入人体的蚕丝生物传感器上。

creators.name: Colleen Flanigan
creators.role: Artist; founder of Living Sea Sculpture
creators.bio: American sculptor who makes electrified steel structures that grow limestone underwater and serve as coral nurseries.
creators.why: Her sculptures are habitats first: the work is finished by corals and fish.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；Living Sea Sculpture 创始人
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家，制作通电的钢结构，在水下长出石灰岩，成为珊瑚苗圃。
creators.why_zh: 她的雕塑首先是栖息地：作品由珊瑚和鱼来完成。

creators.name: Next Nature Network
creators.role: Design and research organisation founded by Koert van Mensvoort
creators.bio: Dutch network that uses design fiction, exhibitions and campaigns to discuss technology that becomes as complex and autonomous as nature.
creators.why: Projects such as Bistro In Vitro and Rayfish Footwear test public reactions to lab-grown meat and custom-engineered animals.
creators.role_zh: 由 Koert van Mensvoort 创立的设计与研究机构
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰机构，用设计虚构、展览和公共活动讨论那些变得像自然一样复杂而自主的技术。
creators.why_zh: Bistro In Vitro 和 Rayfish Footwear 等项目测试公众对实验室培养肉和定制基因动物的反应。

creators.name: Eduardo Navarro
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Argentine artist whose performances and drawings invite people to take on the perception of plants, animals and other beings.
creators.why: He collaborates with philosopher Michael Marder on works that practise 'vegetal' thinking.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.based_zh: 布宜诺斯艾利斯，阿根廷
creators.bio_zh: 阿根廷艺术家，通过表演和绘画邀请人们体验植物、动物和其他生命的感知方式。
creators.why_zh: 他与哲学家 Michael Marder 合作，创作练习“植物性”思考的作品。

creators.name: Patricia Domínguez
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Chilean artist whose installations combine ethnobotany, healing practices and digital media to question colonial relationships with plants.
creators.why: Her work honours Indigenous plant knowledge alongside the archives that extracted it.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 智利艺术家，装置作品把民族植物学、疗愈实践与数字媒体结合，质疑与植物之间的殖民关系。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品把原住民的植物知识与攫取这些知识的档案并置，并向前者致敬。

creators.name: Rachel Mayeri
creators.role: Artist and filmmaker; Professor of Media Studies, Harvey Mudd College
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、电影人；Harvey Mudd College 媒体研究教授
creators.bio: Rachel Mayeri makes films and installations at the edge of art and primatology, including the Primate Cinema series of films made for chimpanzee and baboon audiences.
creators.bio_zh: Rachel Mayeri 在艺术与灵长类学的交界处创作电影和装置，代表作是为黑猩猩和狒狒观众拍摄的《Primate Cinema》系列。
creators.why: She asks what cinema looks like when another species is the audience.
creators.why_zh: 她追问：当观众是另一个物种时，电影会是什么样子。

creators.name: François-Joseph Lapointe
creators.role: Biologist and performance artist; Professor, Université de Montréal
creators.role_zh: 生物学家、行为艺术家；蒙特利尔大学教授
creators.bio: François-Joseph Lapointe is an evolutionary biologist who uses DNA sequencing of his own microbiome as material for performances and portraits.
creators.bio_zh: François-Joseph Lapointe 是进化生物学家，他把对自身微生物组的 DNA 测序用作行为艺术和肖像的材料。
creators.why: His work shows the human body as a shifting community of microbes shaped by contact with others.
creators.why_zh: 他的作品把人体呈现为一个随与他人接触而不断变化的微生物群落。

creators.name: Vivian Xu
creators.role: Media artist and researcher working between bio and electronic media
creators.role_zh: 在生物媒介与电子媒介之间工作的媒体艺术家、研究者
creators.bio: Vivian Xu builds hybrid machines and wearables that combine insects such as silkworms with electronics and computation.
creators.bio_zh: Vivian Xu（徐薇）把蚕等昆虫与电子和计算结合，制作混合机器和可穿戴装置。
creators.why: Her silk machines treat insect behaviour as a basis for technological design.
creators.why_zh: 她的造丝机器把昆虫行为当作技术设计的基础。

creators.name: Nigel Helyer
creators.role: Sculptor and sound artist (a.k.a. Dr Sonique)
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家、声音艺术家（又名 Dr Sonique）
creators.bio: Nigel Helyer makes large sonic installations and bio-acoustic works, and was an early artist in residence at SymbioticA (2002–03).
creators.bio_zh: Nigel Helyer 创作大型声音装置和生物声学作品，2002–03 年曾在 SymbioticA 驻留。
creators.why: He uses animal nervous systems as microphones to shift the listening position away from humans.
creators.why_zh: 他把动物的神经系统当作麦克风，把聆听的位置从人身上移开。

creators.name: Tagny Duff
creators.role: Artist-researcher and curator
creators.role_zh: 艺术研究者、策展人
creators.bio: Tagny Duff works with tissue culture, viruses and bookbinding to explore how biotechnology archives and transmits life.
creators.bio_zh: Tagny Duff 以组织培养、病毒和装订工艺探讨生物技术如何存档和传递生命。
creators.why: She treats viral transfection as a form of writing and documentation.
creators.why_zh: 她把病毒转染看作一种书写和记录方式。

creators.name: ORLAN
creators.role: Artist working with performance, surgery and biotechnology
creators.role_zh: 以表演、外科手术和生物技术创作的艺术家
creators.bio: ORLAN is a French artist known for her surgery-performances of the 1990s and for later work with cell culture and biotechnology.
creators.bio_zh: ORLAN 是法国艺术家，以 1990 年代的外科手术表演闻名，后来转向细胞培养和生物技术创作。
creators.why: She uses the body's own cells to question identity, ownership and hybridity.
creators.why_zh: 她用身体自己的细胞追问身份、所有权与混杂。

creators.name: Christian Brems
creators.role: Artist
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio: Christian Brems is a Danish artist working with sound, plants and speculative bio-acoustics.
creators.bio_zh: Christian Brems 是丹麦艺术家，以声音、植物和思辨生物声学为创作题材。
creators.why: He takes new findings on plant hearing as material for installations.
creators.why_zh: 他把关于植物“听觉”的新研究当作装置的材料。

creators.name: Antti Tenetz
creators.role: Artist working with animals, landscape and tracking technology
creators.role_zh: 以动物、景观和追踪技术创作的艺术家
creators.bio: Antti Tenetz makes videos and installations from GPS tracks, drone and underwater footage of wild animals in northern landscapes.
creators.bio_zh: Antti Tenetz 用野生动物的 GPS 轨迹、无人机和水下影像，创作关于北方景观的影像和装置。
creators.why: He makes the presence of animals in a landscape visible through their own movements.
creators.why_zh: 他通过动物自身的移动，让它们在景观中的存在变得可见。

creators.name: MAEID
creators.role: Büro für Architektur und Transmediale Kunst (Daniela Mitterberger, Tiziano Derme)
creators.role_zh: 建筑与跨媒体艺术事务所（Daniela Mitterberger、Tiziano Derme）
creators.bio: MAEID is an architecture and media art office that builds robotic, soil-based and living environments.
creators.bio_zh: MAEID 是一家建筑与媒体艺术事务所，建造以机器人、土壤和活体系统为基础的环境。
creators.why: Their work makes robots caretakers of soil and fungal life in architecture.
creators.why_zh: 他们的作品让机器人成为建筑中土壤和真菌生命的照料者。

creators.name: doxiadis+
creators.role: Landscape architecture office led by Thomas Doxiadis
creators.role_zh: 由 Thomas Doxiadis 主持的景观建筑事务所
creators.bio: doxiadis+ is a Greek landscape and architecture practice working on ecological landscapes, drylands and multispecies design.
creators.bio_zh: doxiadis+ 是希腊的景观与建筑事务所，关注生态景观、干旱地区与多物种设计。
creators.why: They bring fungi, usually invisible, into the discussion of how to live together.
creators.why_zh: 他们把通常看不见的真菌带进“如何共同生活”的讨论。

creators.name: Rasa Smite & Raitis Smits
creators.role: Artist duo; founders of RIXC Center for New Media Culture
creators.role_zh: 艺术家二人组；RIXC 新媒体文化中心创办人
creators.bio: Rasa Smite and Raitis Smits make networked and data-based installations about forests, climate and the atmosphere.
creators.bio_zh: Rasa Smite 和 Raitis Smits 创作以森林、气候和大气为题的联网与数据装置。
creators.why: They render the gas exchange of trees as an experience people can enter.
creators.why_zh: 他们把树木的气体交换变成人可以进入的体验。

creators.name: Nomeda & Gediminas Urbonas
creators.role: Artist duo; Gediminas Urbonas is Professor at MIT
creators.role_zh: 艺术家二人组；Gediminas Urbonas 为 MIT 教授
creators.based_zh: 维尔纽斯，立陶宛 / 剑桥，美国
creators.bio: Nomeda and Gediminas Urbonas run long-term projects on swamps, rivers and commons, including the Swamp School at the Venice Biennale 2018.
creators.bio_zh: Nomeda 和 Gediminas Urbonas 长期开展关于沼泽、河流与公共资源的项目，包括 2018 年威尼斯双年展的 Swamp School。
creators.why: They propose the swamp as a model for thinking with more-than-human ecologies.
creators.why_zh: 他们把沼泽当作与超越人类的生态一起思考的模型。

creators.name: Sybille Neumeyer
creators.role: Artist and researcher
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者
creators.bio: Sybille Neumeyer works on insects, viruses and environmental data, combining archives, specimens and field research.
creators.bio_zh: Sybille Neumeyer 以昆虫、病毒和环境数据为题，结合档案、标本和田野研究进行创作。
creators.why: She follows how insects turn into specimens, bioindicators and data.
creators.why_zh: 她追踪昆虫如何变成标本、生物指示物和数据。

creators.name: Werewool
creators.role: Biotech fibre start-up co-founded by Chui-Lian Lee and Valentina Gomez
creators.bio: Werewool designs textile fibres from protein sequences found in nature, such as fluorescent coral proteins, so that colour, stretch or moisture handling are built into the fibre itself.
creators.why: Treats the gene sequence as the design material for a fibre: properties are chosen at the DNA level instead of added with dyes and finishes.
creators.role_zh: 由 Chui-Lian Lee 和 Valentina Gomez 共同创立的生物纤维初创公司
creators.bio_zh: Werewool 从自然界的蛋白质序列（例如珊瑚的荧光蛋白）出发设计纺织纤维，让颜色、弹性或吸湿性直接内置于纤维本身。
creators.why_zh: 把基因序列当作纤维的设计材料：性能在 DNA 层面就被选定，而不是靠染料和后整理加上去。

creators.name: TômTex
creators.role: Materials start-up founded by designer Uyen Tran
creators.bio: TômTex makes a plastic-free leather alternative from chitosan extracted from seafood shells and mushroom waste; it started as Uyen Tran's student project at Pratt Institute.
creators.why: A material that uses food-industry waste and fungal chitin instead of plastic binders, showing a low-tech route to bio-based leather.
creators.role_zh: 由设计师 Uyen Tran 创立的材料初创公司
creators.bio_zh: TômTex 用从海鲜壳和蘑菇废料中提取的壳聚糖制作不含塑料的皮革替代品，最初是 Uyen Tran 在普瑞特艺术学院的学生项目。
creators.why_zh: 用食品工业废料和真菌甲壳素代替塑料黏合剂，展示了一条相对低技术门槛的生物基皮革路线。

creators.name: Polybion
creators.role: Bacterial-cellulose materials company founded by brothers Axel and Alexis Gómez-Ortigoza
creators.bio: Polybion grows Celium, a leather-like bacterial cellulose sheet, by feeding bacteria with fruit waste from Mexican agro-industry in large fermentation facilities.
creators.why: One of the first companies to scale bacterial cellulose from a kitchen-table kombucha experiment to an industrial material.
creators.role_zh: 由 Axel 与 Alexis Gómez-Ortigoza 兄弟创立的细菌纤维素材料公司
creators.bio_zh: Polybion 用墨西哥农产品加工留下的水果废料喂养细菌，在大型发酵设施中生长出名为 Celium 的类皮革细菌纤维素片材。
creators.why_zh: 最早把细菌纤维素从类似康普茶的桌面实验放大为工业材料的公司之一。

creators.name: Malai
creators.role: Biomaterials studio founded by Zuzana Gombošová and CS Susmith
creators.bio: Malai grows bacterial cellulose on waste coconut water collected from coconut processors in Kerala and turns it into a flexible, leather-like material for bags and accessories.
creators.why: Links a local agricultural by-product to a grown material, a model for biofabrication outside high-tech labs.
creators.role_zh: 由 Zuzana Gombošová 和 CS Susmith 创立的生物材料工作室
creators.bio_zh: Malai 用从喀拉拉邦椰子加工厂收集的废弃椰子水培养细菌纤维素，再做成柔韧的类皮革材料，用于包袋和配饰。
creators.why_zh: 把本地农业副产品和生长材料联系起来，是在高科技实验室之外开展生物制造的范例。

creators.name: Lucy Hughes
creators.role: Product designer; founder of MarinaTex
creators.bio: Lucy Hughes developed MarinaTex as her final-year product design project at the University of Sussex and won the 2019 James Dyson Award with it.
creators.why: Her work shows how fishing-industry waste and seaweed can be combined into a home-compostable film to replace single-use plastic.
creators.role_zh: 产品设计师，MarinaTex 创始人
creators.bio_zh: Lucy Hughes 在萨塞克斯大学的毕业设计中开发了 MarinaTex，并凭此获得 2019 年詹姆斯·戴森设计奖。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品展示了渔业废料和海藻如何结合成可家庭堆肥的薄膜，用来替代一次性塑料。

creators.name: Elissa Brunato
creators.role: Material designer; graduate of the MA Material Futures, Central Saint Martins
creators.bio: Elissa Brunato works on bio-based alternatives for fashion embellishment; her Bio Iridescent Sequin was developed with RISE Research Institutes of Sweden.
creators.why: Shows that colour can come from structure grown into a plant-derived material rather than from pigments or plastic coatings.
creators.role_zh: 材料设计师，毕业于中央圣马丁 MA Material Futures
creators.bio_zh: Elissa Brunato 研究时尚装饰的生物基替代品，她的 Bio Iridescent Sequin 与瑞典 RISE 研究院合作开发。
creators.why_zh: 展示了颜色可以来自植物来源材料内部的结构，而不是颜料或塑料涂层。

creators.name: Tandem Repeat
creators.role: Biotech textile company co-founded by Melik Demirel and Gözde Senel-Ayaz
creators.bio: A Penn State spin-out that produces Squitex, a protein fibre based on the tandem-repeat structure of squid ring teeth, made by microbial fermentation.
creators.why: Takes a molecular structure from an animal as a template and grows it in microbes to get self-healing, biodegradable textiles.
creators.role_zh: 由 Melik Demirel 和 Gözde Senel-Ayaz 共同创立的生物技术纺织公司
creators.based_zh: 美国宾夕法尼亚州州立学院
creators.bio_zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的衍生公司，用微生物发酵生产 Squitex——一种基于鱿鱼吸盘环齿蛋白串联重复结构的蛋白质纤维。
creators.why_zh: 以动物的分子结构为模板，在微生物中“长”出可自愈、可降解的纺织材料。

creators.name: Tina Gorjanc
creators.role: Slovenian designer and researcher; graduate of the MA Material Futures, Central Saint Martins
creators.bio: Tina Gorjanc works on the legal and ethical side of biotechnology in fashion, using speculative prototypes to expose gaps in the protection of genetic information.
creators.why: Her work makes the ownership of biological material, not only its fabrication, a design question.
creators.role_zh: 斯洛文尼亚设计师与研究者，毕业于中央圣马丁 MA Material Futures
creators.bio_zh: Tina Gorjanc 研究时尚领域生物技术的法律与伦理问题，用思辨原型揭示遗传信息保护中的漏洞。
creators.why_zh: 她让“谁拥有生物材料”而不仅是“如何制造”成为设计问题。

creators.name: Jonathan Dessi-Olive
creators.role: Architect; Assistant Professor of Architecture, University of North Carolina at Charlotte
creators.bio: Jonathan Dessi-Olive designs and grows large structures from mycelium composites, from the vaulted Monolito Micelio pavilion (2018) to the suspended acoustic sculpture Phoenix (2023).
creators.why: He pushes mycelium from bricks and panels to building-scale forms, combining computational design with cultivation.
creators.role_zh: 建筑师，北卡罗来纳大学夏洛特分校建筑学助理教授
creators.based_zh: 美国北卡罗来纳州夏洛特
creators.bio_zh: Jonathan Dessi-Olive 用菌丝体复合材料设计并生长大型结构，从拱形展亭 Monolito Micelio（2018）到悬挂式声学雕塑 Phoenix（2023）。
creators.why_zh: 他把菌丝体从砖块和板材推进到建筑尺度的形态，把计算设计和培养过程结合起来。

creators.name: Natalie Alima
creators.role: Architect and researcher at the School of Architecture and Urban Design, RMIT University
creators.bio: Natalie Alima develops 'interspecies forms' in which robotically 3D-printed scaffolds are colonised by mycelium, using agent-based algorithms to shape the printed skins.
creators.why: Her work treats the robot and the fungus as co-fabricators of architectural components.
creators.role_zh: 皇家墨尔本理工大学建筑与城市设计学院的建筑师和研究者
creators.bio_zh: Natalie Alima 发展出“跨物种形态”：由机器人 3D 打印的支架被菌丝体占据生长，打印外壳的形态由基于智能体的算法生成。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品把机器人和真菌当作建筑构件的共同制造者。

creators.name: Carolina De Lara
creators.role: Textile designer and biodesign researcher (University of Borås; Kyoto Institute of Technology)
creators.bio: Carolina De Lara works on bacterial cellulose textiles, combining broken-down cellulose fibres with knitted and crocheted structures.
creators.why: She explores bacterial cellulose as a fibre to be reassembled with textile craft, not only as a grown sheet.
creators.role_zh: 纺织设计师与生物设计研究者（布罗斯大学；京都工艺纤维大学）
creators.bio_zh: Carolina De Lara 研究细菌纤维素纺织品，把打散的纤维素纤维与针织、钩织结构结合在一起。
creators.why_zh: 她把细菌纤维素当作可以用纺织手艺重新组合的纤维，而不只是长出来的一张膜。

creators.name: Perla Armaly
creators.role: Architect and biodesign researcher at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
creators.bio: Perla Armaly develops co-fabrication workflows in which robots deposit sand-based mixtures and cyanobacteria mineralise them.
creators.why: Her work shows how living bacteria can be built into an architectural fabrication process rather than added afterwards.
creators.role_zh: 以色列理工学院的建筑师与生物设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Perla Armaly 研究“协同制造”流程：机器人沉积以沙为主的混合料，再由蓝细菌让它矿化。
creators.why_zh: 她的工作展示了活细菌如何被纳入建筑制造流程本身，而不是事后再添加。

creators.name: Aurélie Mosse
creators.role: Designer and researcher; associate professor at EnsadLab, École des Arts Décoratifs, Paris; leads ImpressioVivo
creators.bio: Aurélie Mosse works on responsive and bio-sourced materials; her project ImpressioVivo combines 3D printing and bacterially induced calcification to make circular materials.
creators.why: She brings microbially induced mineralisation from civil engineering into material and product design.
creators.role_zh: 设计师与研究者，巴黎国立高等装饰艺术学院 EnsadLab 副教授，ImpressioVivo 项目负责人
creators.bio_zh: Aurélie Mosse 研究响应性材料和生物来源材料，她的 ImpressioVivo 项目把 3D 打印与细菌诱导钙化结合，制造可循环材料。
creators.why_zh: 她把土木工程中的微生物诱导矿化引入材料与产品设计。

creators.name: Rasa Weber
creators.role: Designer and researcher at Zurich University of the Arts (Interfacing the Ocean) and the Cluster of Excellence Matters of Activity, Berlin
creators.bio: Rasa Weber designs artificial reef structures and underwater habitats with marine biologists, testing prototypes in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean in her doctoral project Symbiocean.
creators.why: She moves biodesign from materials to habitats, designing structures that other species will live on and change.
creators.role_zh: 设计师与研究者，任职于苏黎世艺术大学（Interfacing the Ocean 项目）和柏林卓越集群 Matters of Activity
creators.based_zh: 瑞士苏黎世 / 德国柏林
creators.bio_zh: Rasa Weber 与海洋生物学家合作设计人工礁体结构和水下栖息地，在博士项目 Symbiocean 中于地中海和加勒比海测试原型。
creators.why_zh: 她把生物设计从材料推向栖息地：设计出的结构将由其他物种栖居并改造。

creators.name: Basse Stittgen
creators.role: Designer; tutor in the Social Design master at Design Academy Eindhoven
creators.bio: Basse Stittgen graduated from Design Academy Eindhoven in 2017 and turns overlooked waste streams, such as slaughterhouse blood and urban wood, into objects that make hidden processes visible.
creators.why: His work uses the material itself to open a conversation about how humans use animal bodies.
creators.role_zh: 设计师，埃因霍温设计学院 Social Design 硕士项目导师
creators.bio_zh: Basse Stittgen 于 2017 年毕业于埃因霍温设计学院，把屠宰场血液、城市木材等被忽视的废料转化为物件，让隐藏的过程变得可见。
creators.why_zh: 他用材料本身开启关于人类如何利用动物身体的讨论。

creators.name: Tamara Orjola
creators.role: Designer; graduate of Design Academy Eindhoven (2016)
creators.bio: Tamara Orjola researches unused parts of plants as material; her graduation project Forest Wool turns discarded pine needles into textiles, composites and paper.
creators.why: She shows how a by-product of forestry can become a fibre industry of its own.
creators.role_zh: 设计师，2016 年毕业于埃因霍温设计学院
creators.bio_zh: Tamara Orjola 研究植物中未被利用的部分作为材料；她的毕业项目 Forest Wool 把废弃的松针变成纺织品、复合材料和纸。
creators.why_zh: 她展示了林业的副产品如何发展成一个独立的纤维产业。

creators.name: Madalina Nicolae
creators.role: HCI researcher (Saarland University, Télécom Paris and Léonard de Vinci Pôle Universitaire)
creators.bio: Madalina Nicolae works on growable interactive devices, embedding electronics in living biofilms and bacterial cellulose so that the device body is grown rather than moulded.
creators.why: Her work brings biofabrication into HCI prototyping and proposes growth as a manufacturing process for electronics.
creators.role_zh: 人机交互研究者（萨尔大学、巴黎电信学院与莱昂纳多·达·芬奇大学中心）
creators.bio_zh: Madalina Nicolae 研究可生长的交互设备，把电子元件嵌入活的生物膜和细菌纤维素中，让设备的外壳“长”出来而不是模压出来。
creators.why_zh: 她把生物制造引入人机交互原型设计，提出以生长作为电子产品的制造方式。

creators.name: Arne Hendriks
creators.role: Artist and researcher; long-term collaborator of Mediamatic
creators.bio: Arne Hendriks works on speculative and practical projects about living with less, including The Incredible Shrinking Man and a series of mycelium pigeon towers built with Mediamatic.
creators.why: He uses fungal waste to build temporary architecture for non-human city dwellers.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家与研究者，Mediamatic 的长期合作者
creators.bio_zh: Arne Hendriks 从事关于“少即是多”的思辨与实践项目，包括 The Incredible Shrinking Man，以及与 Mediamatic 合作建造的一系列菌丝体鸽塔。
creators.why_zh: 他用真菌废料为城市中的非人类居民建造临时建筑。

creators.name: Nikoletta Karastathi
creators.role: Textile designer and researcher in biodesign, University College London
creators.bio: Nikoletta Karastathi develops knitted bio-textiles and responsive yarns, including algae-infused wearables and pH-responsive hydrogel yarns.
creators.why: Her work links knitting craft with living and biologically active materials.
creators.role_zh: 伦敦大学学院的纺织设计师与生物设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Nikoletta Karastathi 开发针织生物纺织品和响应性纱线，包括注入藻类的可穿戴物和 pH 响应水凝胶纱线。
creators.why_zh: 她的工作把针织手艺与活体及生物活性材料联系起来。

creators.name: Julian Abraham 'Togar'
creators.role: Artist, musician and self-described pseudo-scientist
creators.bio: Born in Medan in 1987, Julian Abraham 'Togar' makes installations and workshops that connect sound, open-source electronics, fermentation and ecology; he was shortlisted for the Future Generation Art Prize 2024.
creators.why: He uses DIY biology and fermentation workshops to put lab knowledge in the hands of communities.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、音乐人、自称“伪科学家”
creators.bio_zh: Julian Abraham“Togar”1987 年生于棉兰，创作连接声音、开源电子、发酵与生态的装置和工作坊；曾入围 2024 年 Future Generation Art Prize。
creators.why_zh: 他通过 DIY 生物学和发酵工作坊，把实验室知识交到社区手中。

creators.name: Kevin Blackistone
creators.role: Artist and researcher, University of Arts and Design Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz)
creators.bio: Kevin Blackistone builds installations that combine living microbial cultures with robotics and automated imaging.
creators.why: His work uses bacterial growth as a small-scale model for how human populations expand and consume resources.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家与研究者，林茨艺术设计大学
creators.bio_zh: Kevin Blackistone 创作把活体微生物培养与机器人和自动成像结合起来的装置。
creators.why_zh: 他用细菌的生长作为缩微模型，映射人类种群如何扩张并消耗资源。

creators.name: Zeefier
creators.role: Seaweed-dye company founded by designers Nienke Hoogvliet and Anne Boermans
creators.bio: Zeefier scales up Nienke Hoogvliet's seaweed-dye research from SEA ME into natural textile colours made from 100 percent seaweed and its waste streams.
creators.why: Shows a studio research project growing into a supply chain for colour from the sea.
creators.role_zh: 由设计师 Nienke Hoogvliet 和 Anne Boermans 创立的海藻染料公司
creators.bio_zh: Zeefier 把 Nienke Hoogvliet 从 SEA ME 开始的海藻染料研究放大，生产完全由海藻及其废料制成的天然纺织色彩。
creators.why_zh: 展示了一个工作室研究项目如何发展成来自海洋的色彩供应链。

creators.name: Shijia Huang
creators.role: Designer working on bio-printing and microbial habitats
creators.bio: Shijia Huang presented Microbial Oasis at Dutch Design Week 2024, a speculative design that uses bioprinted human tissue as habitat for microorganisms.
creators.why: Her work reverses the usual direction of biotechnology: the human body is proposed as a donor for other species.
creators.role_zh: 从事生物打印与微生物栖息地设计的设计师
creators.bio_zh: Shijia Huang 在 2024 年荷兰设计周展出了 Microbial Oasis——一个用生物打印的人体组织为微生物提供栖息地的思辨设计。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品反转了生物技术通常的方向：人体被提议为其他物种的“捐赠者”。

works.title: Bel-Air
works.description: A domestic air filter in which a fan pulls room air through a glass chamber holding a living plant, so that the leaves and roots absorb toxic compounds released by paints, glues and plastics.
works.description_zh: 一台家用空气净化器：风扇把室内空气抽进装着活体植物的玻璃舱，由叶片和根系吸收油漆、胶水和塑料释放的有毒化合物。
works.idea_en: An appliance can be a life-support system for a plant that in return cleans the air.
works.idea_zh: 家电可以是一株植物的生命维持系统，植物反过来净化空气。
works.method: Builds on NASA research on plants absorbing volatile organic compounds; air is forced past leaves, soil and roots inside a Pyrex and aluminium enclosure, developed with Harvard scientist David Edwards at Le Laboratoire.
works.method_zh: 基于 NASA 关于植物吸收挥发性有机物的研究；空气被强制流过 Pyrex 玻璃和铝制外壳内的叶片、土壤与根系，与哈佛科学家 David Edwards 在 Le Laboratoire 合作开发。

works.title: O (Oxygen Generator), from the Elements project
works.description: A glass vessel of water and Spirulina algae that monitors the oxygen level of a room and, when it drops, switches on light so the algae photosynthesise and release more oxygen.
works.description_zh: 一只装着水和螺旋藻的玻璃容器，监测房间里的氧气含量；含量下降时就开灯，让藻类光合作用、释放更多氧气。
works.idea_en: A microalgae culture can be treated as a household appliance that responds to the room's needs.
works.idea_zh: 微藻培养物可以被当作一件会回应房间需求的家电。
works.method: An oxymetric probe triggers white LEDs and a magnetic stirrer that keep a Spirulina culture photosynthesising inside a glass and aluminium body.
works.method_zh: 氧含量探头触发白色 LED 和磁力搅拌器，让玻璃铝制外壳中的螺旋藻持续进行光合作用。

works.title: Local River
works.description: A piece of domestic furniture that combines a fish aquarium with a small vegetable garden: live freshwater fish are kept at home until eaten, while their waste fertilises the plants that clean their water.
works.description_zh: 一件家具，把鱼缸和小菜园合在一起：活的淡水鱼养在家里直到被吃掉，鱼的排泄物为植物施肥，植物再净化鱼缸的水。
works.idea_en: A small closed loop of fish and plants brings the food chain, and the question of eating animals, into the living room.
works.idea_zh: 一个由鱼和植物组成的小闭环，把食物链以及“吃动物”这件事带进了客厅。
works.method: Aquaponics at domestic scale: fish tanks connect to plant containers so that nitrogen from fish waste feeds herbs and vegetables, which filter the water.
works.method_zh: 家庭尺度的鱼菜共生：鱼缸与种植容器相连，鱼粪中的氮养活香草和蔬菜，植物再过滤水体。

works.title: Biojewellery
works.description: Couples donated bone cells that were grown in a lab on a ceramic scaffold and then made into wedding rings, so each partner wears a ring grown from the other's bone tissue.
works.description_zh: 几对情侣捐出骨细胞，在实验室里长在陶瓷支架上，再被做成婚戒，于是每个人戴的戒指都由伴侣的骨组织长成。
works.idea_en: Tissue engineering can serve intimate, symbolic objects, not only medicine.
works.idea_zh: 组织工程不只可以服务医学，也可以用来做亲密的、有象征意义的物件。
works.method: Bone cells from wisdom-tooth extractions were cultured on a bioactive hydroxyapatite and tricalcium phosphate scaffold at King's College London, then finished with silver by jewellers.
works.method_zh: 从拔智齿时取得的骨细胞在伦敦国王学院被培养在羟基磷灰石和磷酸三钙生物活性支架上，再由首饰匠用银完成戒指。

works.title: Dressing the Meat of Tomorrow
works.description: A proposal for how lab-grown meat could be shaped: a mobile MRI unit scans the most beautiful farm animals, and their organ cross-sections become moulds for in-vitro meat, shown as sculpted models.
works.description_zh: 一个关于实验室培育肉该做成什么形状的提案：移动核磁共振车在乡间扫描最漂亮的牲畜，把它们器官的断面变成体外培育肉的模具，以雕塑模型呈现。
works.idea_en: Cultured meat needs a designed form that reminds eaters where it came from.
works.idea_zh: 培育肉需要一种被设计出来的外形，提醒吃的人它来自哪里。
works.method: Speculative models in plastisol based on MRI slices of animal organs, responding to the Tissue Culture & Art Project's 'disembodied cuisine'.
works.method_zh: 依据动物器官的核磁共振切片用塑料溶胶制作的思辨模型，回应 Tissue Culture & Art Project 的“离体料理”。

works.title: MyBio
works.description: A set of soft toys of genetically modified and cloned animals, such as a glowing GFP bunny, a spider goat that makes silk protein in its milk and a bioreactor cow, meant to help children discuss biotechnology.
works.description_zh: 一组转基因和克隆动物的毛绒玩偶，比如会发光的 GFP 兔子、奶里含蛛丝蛋白的蜘蛛山羊和“生物反应器”奶牛，用来帮助孩子讨论生物技术。
works.idea_en: Familiar toy forms can make engineered animals discussable at home.
works.idea_zh: 熟悉的玩具形态可以让被改造的动物成为家里能谈论的话题。
works.method: Nylon and polyester plush figures based on real transgenic and xenotransplantation research animals, each with a story of its genetic modification.
works.method_zh: 以真实的转基因和异种移植研究动物为原型的尼龙涤纶毛绒玩偶，每个都附有它被改造的故事。

works.title: Made in Transit (Mushroom Growth Packaging)
works.description: Packaging for specialty oyster mushrooms that keeps them growing during transport, so they are ready to harvest when they reach the shop: a shift from 'best before' to 'ready by'.
works.description_zh: 一种为特色平菇设计的包装，让蘑菇在运输途中继续生长，到店时刚好可以采收：从“保质期至”变成“成熟于”。
works.idea_en: A supply chain can be designed around growth instead of preservation.
works.idea_zh: 供应链可以围绕“生长”而不是“保鲜”来设计。
works.method: PET containers with a foam growth pad and inoculated substrate let mushroom fruiting bodies develop in transit; the consumer harvests just before eating.
works.method_zh: 带泡沫培养垫和接种基质的 PET 容器，让蘑菇子实体在运输中发育；消费者在食用前才采收。

works.title: Nanotopia, from the Future Farm project
works.description: A speculative scenario in which nanotechnology that controls cell growth widens the gap between rich and poor: the rich grow cosmetic features such as long eyelashes, while the poor turn their bodies into farms for pharmaceutical products.
works.description_zh: 一个思辨情景：能控制细胞生长的纳米技术拉大了贫富差距——富人长出超长睫毛之类的美容特征，穷人则把自己的身体变成培育药物产品的农场。
works.idea_en: When bodies can grow products, bodies become a new kind of farmland, with all its inequalities.
works.idea_zh: 当身体能长出产品，身体就成了一种新的农田，也带着农田的一切不平等。
works.method: Photographs and prosthetics made with human hair depict bodies used to cultivate stem cells from fat tissue and other clinical products.
works.method_zh: 用人发制作的假体和摄影，描绘被用来培养脂肪来源干细胞等临床产品的身体。

works.title: The Race, from the Future Farm project
works.description: Objects for a post-antibiotic future that help people re-expose themselves to microbes: re-engineered rugged fingernails where bacteria can grow and hair cages for keeping maggots, crickets and mantises close to the body.
works.description_zh: 为后抗生素时代设计的物件，帮助人重新接触微生物：改造成粗糙表面、让细菌能生长的指甲，以及用头发编成、把蛆虫、蟋蟀和螳螂贴身养着的笼子。
works.idea_en: Instead of more hygiene, design could help us live closer to microbes and animals again.
works.idea_zh: 与其更加卫生，设计也许可以帮我们重新和微生物、动物靠得更近。
works.method: Speculative prototypes in resin, silicone, wood, wire, hair and a taxidermy mantis, based on the hygiene hypothesis and antibiotic resistance.
works.method_zh: 基于卫生假说与抗生素耐药性，用树脂、硅胶、木、金属丝、头发和螳螂标本制作的思辨原型。

works.title: Augmented Animals (LED Dog Tail Communicator)
works.description: A series of devices imagining technology designed for animals' own use; the LED Dog Tail Communicator reads the speed of a dog's wagging tail and spells out its message in words for people.
works.description_zh: 一组设想“为动物本身设计的技术”的装置；其中 LED 狗尾巴翻译器读取狗摇尾巴的速度，把它想表达的意思用文字显示给人看。
works.idea_en: Ask what gadgets would exist if animals were the users, to expose how human-centred technology is.
works.idea_zh: 问一问：如果动物是用户，会出现哪些小工具？以此揭示技术有多么以人为中心。
works.method: An automated wagging tail fitted with programmed LEDs maps tail speed to text; other concepts in the series include rodent night-vision goggles and bird-mounted anti-collision radar.
works.method_zh: 装有可编程 LED 的自动摇摆尾巴，把摇尾速度映射成文字；系列中的其他概念还包括老鼠夜视镜和鸟用防撞雷达。

works.title: Totomoxtle
works.description: A veneer for furniture and wall panels made from the purple, red and cream husks of native Mexican corn, grown by a farming community in Tonahuixtla, Puebla, that restores heirloom seed varieties.
works.description_zh: 一种用于家具和墙板的饰面材料，由墨西哥本土玉米的紫、红、米色苞叶制成；这些玉米由普埃布拉州 Tonahuixtla 的农民社区种植，他们同时在恢复传统种子品种。
works.idea_en: A material project can keep a crop's genetic diversity and a community's livelihood alive.
works.idea_zh: 一个材料项目可以同时延续一种作物的遗传多样性和一个社区的生计。
works.method: Heirloom corn is replanted with local farmers; the husks are flattened, ironed onto a textile or paper backing and hand-cut into marquetry.
works.method_zh: 与当地农民重新种植传统玉米品种；把苞叶压平、熨贴在布或纸衬底上，再手工切割拼成镶嵌图案。

works.title: Think Evolution #1: Kiku-ishi (Ammonite)
works.description: Inomata reconstructed ammonite shells from CT scans of a fossil, 3D-printed them in resin and offered them to a living octopus, which moved in and used the shell as a home.
works.description_zh: Inomata 根据化石的 CT 扫描复原了菊石的壳，用树脂 3D 打印出来，送给一只活章鱼；章鱼住了进去，把壳当作自己的家。
works.idea_en: A designed object can stage an encounter between a living animal and its extinct relative.
works.idea_zh: 一件被设计出来的物件，可以让一只活着的动物和它已灭绝的近亲相遇。
works.method: CT data of an ammonite fossil were modelled in 3D CG and printed in transparent resin; the octopus's behaviour with the shell was filmed.
works.method_zh: 菊石化石的 CT 数据经三维建模后用透明树脂打印；拍摄章鱼与壳互动的过程。

works.title: Tissue Printing (multivascular networks)
works.description: Generative designs of intertwined airway and blood-vessel networks printed in soft hydrogels, including a lung-like air sac that oxygenates red blood cells as it breathes.
works.description_zh: 用生成式设计得到彼此缠绕的气道与血管网络，打印在柔软的水凝胶中，其中一个类似肺泡的气囊在“呼吸”时能给红细胞供氧。
works.idea_en: Algorithms that grow forms like nature can give engineered tissue the complex plumbing it needs.
works.idea_zh: 像自然那样“生长”形态的算法，可以为工程组织提供它所需要的复杂管道。
works.method: Projection stereolithography with food-dye photoabsorbers prints entangled vascular architectures in biocompatible PEGDA hydrogels; network topologies were generated by Nervous System with Jordan Miller's lab at Rice University.
works.method_zh: 用食用色素作为光吸收剂的投影立体光刻，在生物相容的 PEGDA 水凝胶中打印相互缠绕的血管结构；网络拓扑由 Nervous System 与莱斯大学 Jordan Miller 实验室合作生成。

paper.title: Multivascular networks and functional intravascular topologies within biocompatible hydrogels

works.title: Living Seawalls
works.description: Hexagonal habitat tiles fixed onto existing flat seawalls whose rock-like textures give oysters, barnacles, seaweed and fish places to settle and hide, raising biodiversity on urban shorelines.
works.description_zh: 一种安装在既有平直海堤上的六边形栖息砖，仿岩石的纹理给牡蛎、藤壶、海藻和鱼提供附着和躲藏的地方，提升城市海岸的生物多样性。
works.idea_en: Grey infrastructure can be retrofitted into habitat with a tile system.
works.idea_zh: 灰色基础设施可以用一套瓷砖系统改造成栖息地。
works.method: Ten 3D-modelled textures are cast in low-carbon concrete with composite reinforcement and bolted to seawalls; colonisation is monitored by the Sydney Institute of Marine Science.
works.method_zh: 十种三维建模的纹理用低碳混凝土和复合筋浇筑后固定在海堤上；由悉尼海洋科学研究所监测生物附着情况。

works.title: Curiosity Cloud
works.description: An installation of hundreds of glass bulbs, each holding a hand-made replica of a different insect species; when visitors approach, the insects start to flutter and tap against the glass, and fall still when people leave.
works.description_zh: 一个由数百只玻璃灯泡组成的装置，每只灯泡里都有一种昆虫的手工复制品；观众走近时昆虫开始扑动、敲击玻璃，人离开后又归于平静。
works.idea_en: Interaction can make people notice species they usually ignore, including declining and invasive insects.
works.idea_zh: 互动能让人注意到平时忽视的物种，包括正在减少和正在入侵的昆虫。
works.method: Each bulb contains a motor-driven insect replica and a sensor; proximity triggers movement and sound, and the species mix reflects local, rare and invasive insects.
works.method_zh: 每只灯泡内有电机驱动的昆虫复制品和传感器；靠近会触发动作和声音，物种组合包括本地常见、稀有和入侵昆虫。

works.title: Tree of 40 Fruit
works.description: Single trees grafted with up to 40 varieties of stone fruit, many of them heirloom or rare, so that one tree blossoms in a gradient of white, pink and crimson and bears plums, peaches, apricots, cherries and nectarines.
works.description_zh: 一棵树上嫁接多达 40 个核果品种，其中许多是传统或稀有品种；一棵树开出白、粉、深红渐变的花，结出李子、桃、杏、樱桃和油桃。
works.idea_en: An orchard's diversity can be compressed into one living sculpture that also preserves rare varieties.
works.idea_zh: 一整片果园的多样性可以浓缩进一件活的雕塑，同时保存稀有品种。
works.method: Chip grafting of scion wood onto a host tree over several years, planned with hand-drawn graft maps that set where each variety blossoms.
works.method_zh: 用芽接法在数年里把接穗嫁接到一棵砧木树上，并用手绘嫁接图规划每个品种开花的位置。

works.title: Infinity Burial Suit
works.description: A cotton burial suit embedded with mushroom spores and other microorganisms, meant to help a buried body decompose and to reduce the toxins it releases into the soil.
works.description_zh: 一件嵌有蘑菇孢子和其他微生物的棉质安葬服，用来帮助遗体在土中分解，并减少释放进土壤的有毒物质。
works.idea_en: Burial can be designed as a partnership with fungi that returns the body to the soil.
works.idea_zh: 安葬可以被设计成与真菌的合作，让身体回到土壤。
works.method: Organic cotton suit threaded with a biomix of fungal spores and microbes, first developed by training mushrooms on the artist's own hair, skin and nails.
works.method_zh: 有机棉安葬服中织入真菌孢子和微生物混合物；最初是让蘑菇“学会”分解艺术家自己的头发、皮肤和指甲而开发的。

works.title: BioMess
works.description: Two displays in luxury vitrines: natural history specimens of odd, context-dependent adaptations, and a semi-living hybridoma cell line kept alive in the gallery, questioning the fetish for engineered life.
works.description_zh: 两组放在奢华展柜里的展品：一组是奇特、依赖环境的适应性状的自然史标本，另一组是在展厅里维持存活的“半活体”杂交瘤细胞系，质疑人们对工程化生命的迷恋。
works.idea_en: Life is messier than engineering allows; the most designed life form may be the most dependent one.
works.idea_zh: 生命比工程允许的更凌乱；被设计得最彻底的生命，也许正是最依赖他者的生命。
works.method: Museum specimens are paired with hybridoma cells, a fusion of cancer and immune cells, maintained in a custom bioreactor display case.
works.method_zh: 把博物馆标本与杂交瘤细胞（癌细胞与免疫细胞融合而成）并置，细胞养在特制的生物反应器展柜中。

works.title: Bamboo Theatre
works.description: An open-air theatre in Hengkeng Village, Zhejiang, made by bending and tying living bamboo stalks into a dome; villagers maintain it by removing dead stalks and weaving in new shoots.
works.description_zh: 浙江横坑村的一座露天剧场，把活着的竹子弯折、捆扎成穹顶；村民通过清除枯竹、编入新笋来维护它。
works.idea_en: A building can be a living plant structure that the community keeps growing.
works.idea_zh: 建筑可以是一种活的植物结构，由社区让它不断生长。
works.method: Existing bamboo in a grove is bent inward and bound at the top to form a vault, with no foundations or cut timber; the structure renews itself as bamboo grows.
works.method_zh: 把竹林中原有的竹子向内弯折、在顶部捆扎成拱顶，不用地基也不用砍伐的木料；结构随竹子生长自我更新。

works.title: Into the Island
works.description: Asked to design a museum on Meizhou Island, Fujian, DnA instead proposed small interventions at six sites around the island, each supporting different activities and species and reusing existing structures.
works.description_zh: 受邀在福建湄洲岛设计一座博物馆，DnA 却提出在岛上六处地点做小规模介入，每处支持不同的活动和物种，并尽量利用现有结构。
works.idea_en: The most useful building for an island may be a set of light interventions that let species regenerate.
works.idea_zh: 对一座岛最有用的建筑，也许是一组让物种得以恢复的轻介入。
works.method: Site surveys of coastal ecology guide the reuse of quarries, dykes and abandoned structures as habitat and public space; documented in a film produced with the CCA Montreal.
works.method_zh: 依据海岸生态调查，把采石场、堤坝和废弃结构改作栖息地和公共空间；与蒙特利尔加拿大建筑中心（CCA）合作拍成影片。

works.title: The City of Birds
works.description: A collection of architectural models based on pigeon lofts, bat towers, aviaries, parrot perches, bird feeders and traps, laid out like a city for birds and paired with proposals for new objects that mediate between birds and people.
works.description_zh: 一组建筑模型，取材于鸽舍、蝙蝠塔、鸟舍、鹦鹉栖架、喂鸟器和捕鸟器，排布得像一座给鸟住的城市，并附有调和鸟与人关系的新物件提案。
works.idea_en: The cage, in all its forms, is a vocabulary for the full range of human relations with birds, from care to control.
works.idea_zh: 各种形态的笼子，构成了人与鸟关系的全部词汇，从照护到控制。
works.method: Typological research into bird architecture across history is translated into cast and assembled models and an artists' book, developed at the Van Eyck Academie with Het Nieuwe Instituut.
works.method_zh: 对历史上各类鸟类建筑做类型学研究，转化为铸造和拼装的模型以及一本艺术家书，在 Van Eyck Academie 与 Het Nieuwe Instituut 合作完成。

works.title: Alusta Pavilion
works.description: A pavilion in the courtyard of the Museum of Finnish Architecture and Design Museum Helsinki, built from mass-produced insulating bricks turned on their side, local clay and wood, whose cavities and planted surroundings became homes for insects, plants and fungi.
works.description_zh: 芬兰建筑博物馆与赫尔辛基设计博物馆庭院里的一座展亭，用侧放的量产隔热砖、本地黏土和木材建成，砖孔和周围的种植成了昆虫、植物和真菌的家。
works.idea_en: Ordinary building materials, re-oriented, can shelter pollinators while still sheltering people.
works.idea_zh: 普通建材换个方向摆放，就能在庇护人的同时庇护传粉昆虫。
works.method: Perforated bricks laid sideways serve as insect nests, clay and biochar panels host soil life, and plantings were chosen with University of Helsinki ecologists; changes were observed over several seasons.
works.method_zh: 侧放的多孔砖用作昆虫巢穴，黏土和生物炭板为土壤生物提供栖所，植物由赫尔辛基大学生态学家协助挑选；数个季节里持续观察变化。

paper.title: Exploring Ecological Relationality Through Architectural Practice

works.title: Living Breakwaters
works.description: A chain of rubble-mound breakwaters off the south shore of Staten Island, New York, that slows waves and erosion while its textured 'reef streets' give oysters, fish and other marine life places to live.
works.description_zh: 纽约史坦顿岛南岸外的一串堆石防波堤，在削减波浪与侵蚀的同时，其带纹理的“礁石街道”为牡蛎、鱼类和其他海洋生物提供栖所。
works.idea_en: Coastal defence can be built as habitat, with ecological and community programmes designed in from the start.
works.idea_zh: 海岸防护可以按栖息地来建造，生态和社区项目从一开始就被设计进去。
works.method: Stone breakwaters are armoured with ecologically enhanced concrete units that create tide pools and crevices; oysters from the Billion Oyster Project are seeded on them.
works.method_zh: 石质防波堤外覆经生态强化的混凝土构件，形成潮池和缝隙；并在其上投放 Billion Oyster Project 培育的牡蛎。

works.title: Multispecies Inc.
works.description: A fictional organisation devoted to the flourishing of all species, presented through drawings, objects and booklets of its field equipment, such as a nomadic fog collector, a fog distributor and 'kin-gatherers' for trees and algae.
works.description_zh: 一家致力于让所有物种繁荣的虚构机构，通过绘画、物件和手册展示它的野外装备，比如游牧式集雾器、布雾器，以及为树木和藻类准备的“亲缘采集器”。
works.idea_en: Imagining the tools of a well-meaning multispecies bureaucracy reveals how awkward human care for other species can be.
works.idea_zh: 想象一个善意的多物种官僚机构会用什么工具，能看出人类照护其他物种时有多笨拙。
works.method: Pencil drawings, prototypes and printed matter build the world of a speculative company, based on research into climate adaptation and ecology.
works.method_zh: 以气候适应和生态学研究为基础，用铅笔画、原型和印刷品构建一家思辨公司的世界。

works.title: Habitat (bird façade, insect façade)
works.description: 3D-printed façade panels with openings sized for either nesting birds or solitary insects, made from rice husks and recycled glass powder and tested on a building in Milan with the architects Park Associati.
works.description_zh: 3D 打印的立面板，开口尺寸分别适合筑巢的鸟或独居昆虫，材料为稻壳和回收玻璃粉，并与 Park Associati 建筑事务所合作在米兰一栋建筑上测试。
works.idea_en: A building skin can be designed as nesting infrastructure for urban birds and insects.
works.idea_zh: 建筑表皮可以被设计成城市鸟类和昆虫的筑巢设施。
works.method: A geopolymer of rice husks and recycled glass powder is 3D printed into profiled panels; hole sizes and depths follow the needs of target bird and insect species, and the profiles add insulation.
works.method_zh: 用稻壳和回收玻璃粉制成的地聚合物 3D 打印成带截面的板材；孔的大小和深度依目标鸟类和昆虫的需要而定，截面同时提供隔热。

works.title: Dolphin Embassy
works.description: An unbuilt floating research station where humans and dolphins would live and communicate together, with a land/water living room, chutes for dolphins to swim between floors and a shared navigation pod.
works.description_zh: 一座未建成的漂浮研究站，人和海豚在其中共同生活、彼此交流：有一个陆水两用的起居室、供海豚在楼层之间游动的滑道，以及人和海豚共用的导航舱。
works.idea_en: Treat another intelligent species as a diplomatic partner that deserves its own embassy.
works.idea_zh: 把另一种智慧物种当作外交伙伴，它值得拥有自己的大使馆。
works.method: Drawings, a booklet and research trips to Australia developed a triangular floating structure, influenced by John C. Lilly's human-dolphin communication research.
works.method_zh: 通过图纸、小册子和赴澳大利亚的考察，发展出一个三角形漂浮结构；受 John C. Lilly 人与海豚交流研究的影响。

works.title: The Transspecies Rosette
works.description: A section of building cladding made of ground cork and natural resin that insulates and waterproofs the wall while serving as a substrate for mosses, grasses, fungi and microbes to grow on.
works.description_zh: 一段建筑外墙挂板，由磨碎的软木和天然树脂制成，在为墙体保温防水的同时，也成为苔藓、草、真菌和微生物生长的基底。
works.idea_en: A façade can be a host for other species rather than a barrier against them.
works.idea_zh: 立面可以成为其他物种的宿主，而不是把它们挡在外面的屏障。
works.method: Cork granulate bound with natural resin is moulded into rosette-shaped panels whose porosity lets microbes, fungi and plants colonise them, developed with VIPEQ.
works.method_zh: 用天然树脂黏合的软木颗粒模压成玫瑰花形的板材，其孔隙让微生物、真菌和植物得以定殖，与 VIPEQ 合作开发。

works.title: Kelp Council
works.description: An immersive installation of large seaweed forms, gathered from species in Europe and East Asia and set in a soundscape of rising and falling tide, inviting visitors into a 'council' with kelp.
works.description_zh: 一件沉浸式装置：大型海藻造型取材于欧洲和东亚的多种海藻，置于潮起潮落的声景中，邀请观众加入一场与海带的“议会”。
works.idea_en: Ask what seaweed needs from us before asking what material it can give us.
works.idea_zh: 在问海藻能给我们什么材料之前，先问它需要我们做什么。
works.method: Dried and treated kelp is formed over armatures into sculptural bodies; the soundscape was composed with Ville Aslak Raasakka from tidal recordings.
works.method_zh: 把干燥处理过的海带覆在骨架上塑成雕塑体；声景由 Ville Aslak Raasakka 用潮汐录音合作创作。

works.title: Accalmie and Stool 18
works.description: A table and two stools whose beechwood bases were built first; the offcuts from making them then fed mycelium that grew into the tabletop and seats, now dormant but able to be reactivated for repairs.
works.description_zh: 一张桌子和两张凳子：先做山毛榉木底座，再用加工剩下的边角料喂养菌丝体，让它长成桌面和坐面；菌丝现在处于休眠，但修补时可以重新激活。
works.idea_en: A piece of furniture can grow part of itself from its own production waste, and stay repairable by the same organism.
works.idea_zh: 一件家具可以用自己的生产废料长出一部分自身，并由同一种生物来维持可修复性。
works.method: Beech sawdust and chips from the base are inoculated with fungal mycelium in moulds; after growth the mycelium is dried to dormancy.
works.method_zh: 把底座产生的山毛榉木屑和碎片在模具中接种真菌菌丝体；长成后干燥使菌丝进入休眠。

works.title: The Chair (insect habitats)
works.description: A chair and other forms made of unfired clay and natural binders, pierced with holes sized for solitary bees, wasps and butterflies, so that the intended users of the furniture are insects rather than people.
works.description_zh: 一把椅子和其他一些造型，用未烧制的黏土和天然黏合剂做成，上面的孔洞按独居蜂、胡蜂和蝴蝶的尺寸开凿，家具真正的使用者是昆虫而不是人。
works.idea_en: Take a familiar human object and redesign it for insect users, down to hole size and surface colour.
works.idea_zh: 拿一件熟悉的人类物件，按昆虫使用者重新设计，细到孔径和表面颜色。
works.method: Hole diameters and binder colours were chosen with ecologists Robert Francis and Brandon Mak to attract target insect species in urban settings.
works.method_zh: 孔径和黏合剂颜色与生态学家 Robert Francis 和 Brandon Mak 一起确定，以吸引城市环境中的目标昆虫。

works.title: The Coast Is Not a Line, It's a Zone
works.description: A mixed-media installation built around the sero, a palm-leaf fish fence used by fisherfolk in Kupang Bay, Timor, which lets young fish and shrimp escape; it argues that the coast is a zone shared by many species rather than a line on a map.
works.description_zh: 一件综合媒介装置，围绕帝汶岛古邦湾渔民使用的 sero（一种棕榈叶鱼栅）展开，这种鱼栅会放走幼鱼和小虾；作品认为海岸是许多物种共享的地带，而不是地图上的一条线。
works.idea_en: Vernacular fishing gear can model how to take from an ecosystem while letting it regenerate.
works.idea_zh: 乡土渔具可以示范如何在索取的同时让生态系统得以再生。
works.method: Fieldwork with the fishing community of Kupang Bay, drawings and a section of a sero woven from gewang (Corypha utan) leaves, made with Gillian Bogart as a Design Museum More than Human Fellowship.
works.method_zh: 在古邦湾渔民社区做田野调查，结合绘图和一段用 gewang（贝叶棕）叶编成的 sero 实物，与 Gillian Bogart 合作完成，属于伦敦设计博物馆 More than Human 研究奖助项目。

works.title: The More-Than-Human Rights Mural
works.description: An eight-metre mural listing rivers that have been granted legal rights, in Colombia, Ecuador, New Zealand, India and Peru among others, with excerpts from the court rulings and constitutional texts that protect them, readable through masks.
works.description_zh: 一幅八米长的壁画，列出已被赋予法律权利的河流（包括哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔、新西兰、印度和秘鲁等地），并附上保护它们的判决书和宪法条文摘录，观众要透过面具才能读到。
works.idea_en: Law is a design material: legal personhood can make a river a subject rather than a resource.
works.idea_zh: 法律也是一种设计材料：法律人格可以让一条河成为主体，而不是资源。
works.method: Research by NYU's More-Than-Human Life (MOTH) Program is visualised with designer Elena Landinez on PVC-free wallpaper and acetate masks.
works.method_zh: 纽约大学 More-Than-Human Life（MOTH）项目的研究，由设计师 Elena Landinez 以无 PVC 壁纸和醋酸纤维面具呈现。

works.title: Algaerium Bioprinter
works.description: A domestic prototype that cultivates Chlorella, Spirulina and Haematococcus in glass reservoirs and inkjet-prints the living microalgae as coloured, edible patterns of health food.
works.description_zh: 一台家用原型机：在玻璃容器里培养小球藻、螺旋藻和雨生红球藻，再用喷墨打印把这些活体微藻打印成彩色的可食用图案。
works.idea_en: Algae farming can shrink to a kitchen appliance that prints food on demand.
works.idea_zh: 藻类养殖可以缩小成一台按需打印食物的厨房电器。
works.method: Microalgae cultures act as ink cartridges for an inkjet process adapted with Imperial College London; the colour of each species also signals its nutrients.
works.method_zh: 微藻培养液充当墨盒，喷墨工艺与帝国理工学院合作改造；不同藻种的颜色也对应着它们的营养成分。

works.title: Yamanaka Furniture
works.description: A set of chairs and tools grown from fungal mycelium bound into sawdust, made during a residency at The Workshop Residence in San Francisco.
works.description_zh: 一组用真菌菌丝体与锯末结合长成的椅子和工具，在旧金山 The Workshop Residence 驻地期间制作。
works.idea_en: Furniture can be cast by letting a fungus grow into a mould.
works.idea_zh: 让真菌在模具里生长，就可以“浇铸”出家具。
works.method: Live fungal cells are mixed into pulverised cellulose; within about a week the mycelium binds the aggregate into the mould's shape, and drying stops growth and hardens it.
works.method_zh: 把活的真菌细胞混入粉碎的纤维素中，约一周内菌丝把这些颗粒结合成模具的形状，干燥后停止生长并变硬。

works.title: Biophotovoltaic Moss Table
works.description: A concept table whose top is a grid of potted mosses wired as biophotovoltaic cells, proposing a lamp powered by photosynthesis.
works.description_zh: 一张概念桌，桌面是一格格盆栽苔藓，被连接成生物光伏电池，设想用光合作用给台灯供电。
works.idea_en: Photosynthesis in a houseplant could become a small domestic power source.
works.idea_zh: 室内植物的光合作用，也许能变成家里的小电源。
works.method: In biophotovoltaic devices, electrons released by photosynthesis and by microbes around the moss roots reach an anode; today this can run a clock, not yet the lamp.
works.method_zh: 在生物光伏装置中，光合作用和苔藓根部周围微生物释放的电子被阳极收集；目前能驱动一个时钟，还点不亮台灯。

works.title: Vessel #1 (The Honeycomb Vase)
works.description: A vase of pure beeswax built by about 60,000 honeybees over two months on a skeleton placed inside a hive.
works.description_zh: 一只纯蜂蜡花瓶，由约 6 万只蜜蜂在两个月里，沿着放进蜂箱的骨架筑成。
works.idea_en: Slow prototyping: the designer sets the form, the colony builds the object.
works.idea_zh: 慢速原型：设计师给出形体，由蜂群建造物件。
works.method: An engineered form is placed in a prepared hive; the designer monitors the comb and occasionally intervenes to guide it, much like shaping a bonsai.
works.method_zh: 把设计好的骨架放进准备好的蜂箱，设计师观察蜂巢的生长，不时介入引导，类似修剪盆景。

works.title: HORTUS.PARIS: The Machinic Harvest
works.description: A cyber-garden of photobioreactors hosting micro- and macroalgae from Paris ponds, which visitors kept alive for four months by pumping air in and posting tweets that grew a virtual garden.
works.description_zh: 一座由光生物反应器组成的赛博花园，里面养着来自巴黎池塘的微藻和大型藻；观众在四个月里通过打气和发推文维持它的生长，推文还喂养着一个虚拟花园。
works.idea_en: A garden can be a feedback loop between organisms, visitors and data.
works.idea_zh: 花园可以是生物、观众和数据之间的一条反馈回路。
works.method: Visitors activate air pumps that feed CO2 to the algae, the harvested biomass percolates onto a filtering surface, and sensor data and tweets feed a smartphone-accessible virtual garden.
works.method_zh: 观众启动气泵，为藻类提供二氧化碳；收获的生物质渗落到过滤面上，传感器数据和推文则喂养一个可用手机访问的虚拟花园。

works.title: Packaging That Creates Its Contents
works.description: A concept for a probiotic drink whose cup is formed by light-responsive bacteria; the dormant cup comes alive when filled with water, produces the drink and later composts.
works.description_zh: 一种益生菌饮料的概念：杯子由对光有反应的细菌成形；干燥休眠的杯子注水后苏醒、产出饮料，用几次后可以堆肥。
works.idea_en: Packaging could be the product: the container grows the drink and then disappears.
works.idea_zh: 包装本身可以就是产品：容器长出饮料，然后自己消失。
works.method: Imagines engineered bacteria that aggregate into a solid cup under a specific light wavelength (likely building on light-control work in Wendell Lim's UCSF lab), then metabolise when rehydrated.
works.method_zh: 设想工程细菌在特定波长的光照下聚集成坚固的杯体（借鉴 UCSF Wendell Lim 实验室的光遗传学研究），重新加水后开始代谢。

works.title: Gen2Seat: Genetic Generation Seat
works.description: A full-scale segmented chair whose modules were grown in the Genspace community lab from Reishi mycelium inside computationally designed moulds, skinned with bacterial cellulose.
works.description_zh: 一把全尺寸分段式椅子，各个模块在 Genspace 社区实验室里用灵芝菌丝在计算设计的模具中长成，外层包着细菌纤维素。
works.idea_en: Household products can be grown in parametric moulds and composted after use.
works.idea_zh: 日用品可以在参数化模具里长出来，用完后埋进花园堆肥。
works.method: Ganoderma lucidum mycelium grows through wood chips, gypsum and oat bran in the moulds; an Acetobacter cellulose skin fuses with it into a hard biopolymer.
works.method_zh: 灵芝（Ganoderma lucidum）菌丝在模具中长透木屑、石膏和燕麦麸，外层的醋酸杆菌纤维素与之融合成坚硬的生物聚合物。

works.title: Bio Computation
works.description: Two strains of genetically modified bacteria are grown together in a dish to produce flat composite sheets with rigid and flexible regions, and the process is modelled in software to design panels for an aircraft envelope.
works.description_zh: 把两种转基因细菌放在同一培养皿里共同生长，产出兼有刚性区和柔性区的平面复合片材；再在软件中模拟这一过程，为飞机外壳设计面板。
works.idea_en: Couple a living fabrication process with design optimisation: search the biology, not just the geometry.
works.idea_zh: 把活体制造过程和设计优化连起来：不仅搜索几何形状，也搜索生物参数。
works.method: One strain makes a fabric-like substance and the other a brick-like one; their growth patterns are simulated in Autodesk Maya with custom plug-ins to explore thousands of variants.
works.method_zh: 一种菌产出类似织物的物质，另一种产出类似砖块的物质；在 Autodesk Maya 与自制插件中模拟它们的生长图案，探索数千种变体。

works.title: Seasons of the Void
works.description: Designed fruits for a crewed voyage to Mars, grown by redesigned microorganisms that feed on electricity from sunlight, presented as a catalogue of specimens and journeys.
works.description_zh: 为载人火星航行设计的水果：由重新设计的微生物以阳光发的电为食长成，以标本和航程图录的形式展示。
works.idea_en: If astronauts need GM food, it must also satisfy desire, not just engineering specs.
works.idea_zh: 如果宇航员必须吃转基因食物，它也得满足欲望，而不只是工程指标。
works.method: Speculative objects and images based on electrosynthesis research, in which microbes fix carbon using electrical current instead of photosynthesis; commissioned by the EDF Foundation.
works.method_zh: 基于电合成研究（微生物用电流而非光合作用固定碳）的思辨物件和图像，由 EDF 基金会委托。

works.title: Post Natural History
works.description: A photographic archive of imagined 'neo-beings': animals redesigned by synthetic biology and tissue engineering to cope with climate change, each shown with a short scientific label, including a semi-robotic jellyfish drone that waters drought-stricken land.
works.description_zh: 一组想象中“新生物”的摄影档案：被合成生物学和组织工程改造、以适应气候变化的动物，每张配有简短的科学说明，其中包括一只为干旱土地浇水的半机械水母无人机。
works.idea_en: Present engineered species in the neutral language of a natural history museum to make them feel real.
works.idea_zh: 用自然史博物馆式的中性语言展示工程物种，让它们显得真实。
works.method: Staged photographs and 3D-printed specimens combine real animals with digitally added traits; labels are written with advice from scientists.
works.method_zh: 布景摄影与 3D 打印标本，把真实动物与数字添加的特征结合；说明文字在科学家建议下撰写。

works.title: Nanomagnetic Plants
works.description: Plants whose roots have absorbed magnetic nanoparticles move visibly when an external magnet is brought near, making plant behaviour immediate and interactive.
works.description_zh: 根部吸收了磁性纳米颗粒的植物，在外部磁铁靠近时会明显移动，让植物行为变得即时、可交互。
works.idea_en: Nanoparticles give plants an 'invisible interface' for motion on human timescales.
works.idea_zh: 纳米颗粒给植物加上一层“看不见的界面”，让它们以人类可感知的速度运动。
works.method: Borrowed from stem-cell targeting research at UCL's Centre for Advanced Biomedical Imaging: engineered magnetic nanoparticles bypass root uptake selection and accumulate in the plant, which then responds to a magnet.
works.method_zh: 借鉴伦敦大学学院先进生物医学成像中心的干细胞靶向研究：工程磁性纳米颗粒绕过根系的选择性吸收在植物体内积累，植物随后对磁铁产生反应。

works.title: The Cactus Project
works.description: A living artwork in which a human keratin gene was introduced into cacti, with the aim of making the plants grow hair-like structures in place of spines.
works.description_zh: 一件活体艺术作品：把人类角蛋白基因导入仙人掌，设想让它长出类似毛发的结构来代替刺。
works.idea_en: Transgenic art can make the paradoxes of genetic engineering visible and uncomfortable.
works.idea_zh: 转基因艺术可以让基因工程中的悖论变得可见、令人不安。
works.method: A disarmed Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain (LBA4404) carried the keratin construct into cactus tissue; transformed shoots were regenerated on hormone media and confirmed by PCR and Southern blot.
works.method_zh: 用去毒的根癌农杆菌（LBA4404 株）把角蛋白基因构建体导入仙人掌组织，在激素培养基上再生出转化苗，并用 PCR 和 Southern 印迹验证。

works.title: When I Feel Like Nature May Give Up
works.description: A drawing and film made by dropping protocell-laden ink droplets onto a canvas among sand, stones and burnt wood; the droplets move towards a food source for two to three minutes and leave coloured trails.
works.description_zh: 一幅画和一部影片：把含原细胞的墨滴滴在铺有沙子、石头和焦木的画布上，墨滴在两三分钟里朝“食物源”移动，留下彩色轨迹。
works.idea_en: Lifelike chemistry can become a drawing agent with its own will.
works.idea_zh: 类生命化学可以成为一个有自己“意志”的绘画主体。
works.method: Protocells are chemical droplets (not alive) whose programmed chemistry lets them move and respond to each other; the artist places each colour and films the resulting traces.
works.method_zh: 原细胞是化学液滴（并非生命），其设定好的化学反应让它们移动并彼此回应；艺术家逐一放置各色液滴，并拍下留下的轨迹。

works.title: Amoeba (Protocell Trainer)
works.description: A concept running shoe for 2050 made of a protocell 'skin' that forms around the foot, adds support where impact is high and is revived in a nutrient bath after each run.
works.description_zh: 一双面向 2050 年的概念跑鞋，由在脚上成形的原细胞“皮肤”构成，在冲击大的部位加强支撑，每次跑完后放进营养液里恢复。
works.idea_en: A shoe could be a living, reconfigurable layer that adapts to one runner.
works.idea_zh: 鞋可以是一层活的、可重构的材料，只适应一位跑者。
works.method: Proposes 3D-printed protocells, lifelike chemical droplets that respond to pressure and heat, developed in conversation with protocell scientist Martin Hanczyc.
works.method_zh: 设想 3D 打印的原细胞——能对压力和温度作出反应的类生命化学液滴，与原细胞科学家 Martin Hanczyc 共同讨论发展。

works.title: Plant Fiction
works.description: Five fictional plant species placed in a near-future London, each designed to fix a human-made problem, such as Agave Autovora, a plant that digests itself into biofuel.
works.description_zh: 五种虚构植物被放进近未来的伦敦，每一种都用来修补一个人造问题，比如会把自己消化成生物燃料的 Agave Autovora。
works.idea_en: Imagined plant species expose how utilitarian our view of nature is.
works.idea_zh: 想象中的植物物种，暴露出我们看待自然时的功利眼光。
works.method: Speculative specimens and narratives: plants that turn into biofuel, secrete security pigments, sense airborne viruses or recover gold from electronic waste.
works.method_zh: 思辨性的标本和叙事：会变成生物燃料、分泌防伪色素、感知空气中病毒或从电子垃圾中回收黄金的植物。

works.title: Skinsucka
works.description: A design film in which swarms of bacteria-powered micro-robots clean the home and the skin, then extrude the digested dirt as threads woven into the wearer's clothes.
works.description_zh: 一部设计影片：成群由细菌供能的微型机器人清洁房屋和皮肤，再把消化后的灰尘吐成丝，织进使用者的衣服。
works.idea_en: Living appliances may take over servile work, and we should ask who pays for it.
works.idea_zh: 活体家电可能接手仆役式的劳动，而我们应当追问代价由谁承担。
works.method: Imagines microbial fuel cells that let autonomous micro-devices feed on household dirt; made by Van Heerden Mama with Nancy Tilbury, Bart Hess and others.
works.method_zh: 设想微生物燃料电池让自主微型装置以家中灰尘为食；由 Van Heerden Mama 与 Nancy Tilbury、Bart Hess 等人共同制作。

works.title: eSkin
works.description: A research project designing responsive building-skin materials and sensors from the way human cells sense and remodel their surroundings, shown as petri-dish material prototypes and a lab installation.
works.description_zh: 一个研究项目，从人体细胞感知并改造周围环境的方式出发，设计会响应的建筑表皮材料和传感器，以培养皿材料原型和实验室装置的形式展出。
works.idea_en: Cell behaviour can be a model for building skins that adapt without much energy.
works.idea_zh: 细胞行为可以成为低能耗自适应建筑表皮的模型。
works.method: An NSF-funded collaboration between Cornell and the University of Pennsylvania combining cell-matrix biology, nanoscale materials by Shu Yang and electrical engineering to make optically responsive surfaces.
works.method_zh: 由美国国家科学基金会资助、康奈尔大学与宾夕法尼亚大学合作，把细胞-基质生物学、Shu Yang 的纳米材料和电子工程结合起来，制作光学上可响应的表面。

works.title: The Plasmorph: Living Information
works.description: A short film about a semi-living device that connects to the wearer's nervous system and lets nomadic users ingest information instantly, acting as a living diary.
works.description_zh: 一部短片，讲述一种与佩戴者神经系统相连的半活体装置，让游牧式的使用者即时“摄入”信息，像一本活的日记。
